title: Kaijune Roars In: LEGO Designers Unleash Their Inner Monster Builders
summary: It's Kaijune, the internet's monster-brick tradition, and a couple of actual LEGO set designers have popped up with their own kaiju MOCs. Teal, terrifying and made entirely of plastic.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
June's over but Kaijune's spirit lives on, apparently. You know the drill by now — brick builders spend a month channelling their inner monster movie fan, smashing together scaly, spiky, city-stomping creations for the fun of it. This year's crop is a bit thin on the ground compared to Aquajune's underwater takeover, but two names worth shouting about have joined in: actual LEGO set designers, moonlighting as AFOLs (that's Adult Fans Of LEGO, for the uninitiated).

- **Huib Versteeg**, LEGO Space legend turned pro designer, built **"Knife-Legs"** — a Pacific Rim-style kaiju rumoured (by the community, tongue firmly in cheek) to be Knifehead's smaller cousin. Teal has never looked so menacing.
- **Áron Gerencsér** (known online as Pohaturon) built **"Spikey Boy"**, putting the new Earth Elemental pieces from January's Ninjago wave to genuinely creative use. Small, cute, apparently very dangerous — we'll take their word for it.
- There's also a nod back to **Maxx Davidson's "kawaiiju"** creation from last year, too good not to mention twice.

No official LEGO Group involvement here — these are fan builds (MOCs, or "My Own Creations") shared by builders who happen to also design official sets for a living. No set numbers, no piece counts, no prices — just brick creativity doing its thing.

## Why it matters
It's a lovely reminder that the people designing your favourite official sets are still, underneath it all, the same brick nerds building silly monster mechs for fun in June. If you're hunting for MOC inspiration, or just fancy seeing what happens when Ninjago elemental pieces meet a Pacific Rim mood board, this is worth a scroll.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for whether a proper Kaiju LEGO Ideas set (Godzilla's been floated as a fan favourite) ever gets the official green light — that would be a very different kind of Kaijune altogether.

title: This LEGO Meduseld MOC is the Rohirrim upgrade your Middle-earth shelf needed
summary: Fan builder monsieur.kek has built a huge, gorgeous custom Golden Hall of Rohan, complete with SNOT wood-plank walls, a straw-tile roof and minifigs of Théoden and Éowyn.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
While we're all still admiring official LEGO Minas Tirith, one fan builder has quietly filled a gap the LEGO Group has left wide open since 2012.

MOC creator monsieur.kek has built a massive custom recreation of Meduseld, the Golden Hall of Rohan from Lord of the Rings, and it's a proper stunner. There's been no official Rohirrim set since Battle of Helm's Deep and the Uruk-Hai Army came out over a decade ago, so this build is doing some serious heavy lifting for Rohan fans.

Highlights from the build:
- SNOT (studs-not-on-top) pillars and upper walls that trick your eye into seeing real wooden planks
- Stacked cheese slopes above the golden arches for extra texture on the entrance
- A tan tiled roof echoing the Rivendell set's style, but recoloured to suggest straw thatching
- Side doors made from sideways plates and tiles, styled to look like they'd actually swing open
- A raised stone display platform with smooth tiling but enough exposed studs for minifigs
- Custom Théoden and Éowyn minifigs, with Théoden repurposing the new Unicorn Elf CMF hair piece to great effect

This is a fan-built creation, not an official LEGO product, so you won't find a set number or price tag here. It's built from standard LEGO elements though, which means techniques like these are fair game for your own MOCs.

## Why it matters
Rohan fans have been waiting a long, long time for their kingdom to get some love, and official sets haven't exactly rushed to fill the gap. Builds like this show what's possible with clever part choices and patience, and honestly this might be the closest thing to a proper LEGO Meduseld we'll see for a while. It's also a lovely companion piece if you've already got Minas Tirith taking pride of place on your shelf.

## What to watch next
No word on official LEGO Rohan sets, but Éowyn getting a fan minifig makes us wonder aloud whether LEGO might finally give her the official treatment. We'll keep our eyes peeled for more Middle-earth MOCs and any hints from LEGO's Lord of the Rings line.

title: BrickLink Designer Program swaps 'Series' for 'Waves' from 2028
summary: BrickLink has confirmed a shake-up to how it labels BDP releases from 2028, ditching 'Series' for 'Waves' and giving the packaging a fresh coat of paint.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
BrickLink has dropped official details on the next chapter of the BrickLink Designer Program (BDP), and it's mostly about names and looks rather than new sets themselves.

From the 2028 production year, BrickLink is retiring the word 'Series' in favour of 'Waves'. So what would've been Series 12 becomes **2028 Wave 1** instead. The idea is simple: the year's right there in the name, so you know roughly when your set's shipping without doing sums in your head.

Key bits confirmed by BrickLink:

- New naming kicks in from the **2028 production year** onwards
- Past releases keep their old names - Series 9, 10 and 11 aren't being renamed
- Maximum of **three Waves per year**
- Refreshed BDP icon - still bright orange, but a cleaner 1x1 tile design that scales better
- Boxes go largely blue (matching BrickLink's brand colour), with an accent colour per Wave: **Wave 1 = purple, Wave 2 = green, Wave 3 = red**
- BrickLink says there are **no further changes planned** beyond this naming and packaging refresh
- The programme itself isn't going anywhere - BrickLink confirmed it's continuing to grow

Worth remembering the BDP's history here too - it's been through a fair few makeovers already. Max quantities have crept from 5,000 up to 30,000+, and this is the third naming shift after Rounds became Series and now Series becomes Waves. Builders have also noted designers are now capped at one selection per year to spread the love around a bit more.

## Why it matters
If you're a regular BDP backer, this doesn't change what you can build - it changes how you'll find and track it. Clearer year-based naming should make it easier to spot when a set's actually landing on your doorstep, and the colour-coded packaging means less squinting at box art to work out which Wave you're holding. Handy for anyone building a collection and trying to keep their shelf (and their wallet) organised.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for the first 2028 submissions this Autumn - that's when we'll see the new Wave 1 branding and icon in the wild for real, rather than just in preview shots.

title: LEGO Insiders Days are here: free Sea Serpent, double points and juicy discounts
summary: LEGO.com's annual Insiders Days promos have kicked off, with a free Sea Serpent up for grabs and discounts on sets like the PAC-MAN Arcade — but you'll need to be quick, it all wraps up 12 July.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened

Right, wallets at the ready — LEGO Insiders Days have landed on LEGO.com and there's actually some decent stuff on offer this time.

Here's what's up for grabs:

- **40912 Sea Serpent** – free with any order over £160 / $180 / €180 (this is a proper GWP, not a discount)
- **5010033 Airplane – Special Edition** – free with any Creator, City or Friends purchase over £90 / $100 / €100
- **Double Insiders points** on Sonic the Hedgehog, Jurassic World, Speed Champions, Harry Potter, Marvel, Disney, Wicked and Education sets
- **Discounts** vary by region, but Europe's getting 20% off:
  - 10323 PAC-MAN Arcade
  - 10337 Lamborghini Countach 5000 Quattrovalvole
  - 21360 Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory

Worth noting — one Aussie fan's already reported the Sea Serpent sold out over there, so don't hang about if you fancy one. The whole promo runs until 12 July, or until stock runs dry, whichever comes first.

## Why it matters

Free sets and double points don't come round every week. If you were already planning a big LEGO.com order, timing it during this window could bag you an extra freebie or two without spending a penny more. Classic case of shop smart, not just shop fast.

## What to watch next

Keep an eye on stock levels for the Sea Serpent especially — GWPs have a nasty habit of vanishing before the official end date. Regional discounts may also shift, so it's worth checking your local LEGO.com store rather than assuming the UK gets identical pricing to Europe.

title: LEGO Pokémon just got its first ever minifigures, and there's a Poké Ball to hold them
summary: Five new LEGO Pokémon sets have been officially announced, headlined by a Poké Ball packed with the range's very first minifigures. Pre-orders are live now.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened

Right, put your Poké Balls away, LEGO's just released a real one. The LEGO Group and The Pokémon Company International have officially unveiled five new sets for the LEGO Pokémon range, and this time we're finally getting actual minifigures, not just those big brick-built creature displays.

The big one is the **Iconic Trainer Moments Poké Ball**, a brick-built Poké Ball that opens up to reveal scenes from a Trainer's journey, including a battle and Professor Oak's lab. Inside you get three minifigures (Professor Oak, Picnicker and Red) plus Pikachu and Eevee figures. That's the first proper minifigures this theme has ever had, so yes, it's a genuine moment.

Here's the full pre-order lineup:

- **72154 Iconic Trainer Moments Poké Ball** – 2,339 pieces – £229.99 / $299.99 / €249.99 – includes minifigures of Professor Oak, Picnicker and Red, plus Pikachu and Eevee figures
- **72150 Munchlax** – 757 pieces – £59.99 / $69.99 / €69.99 – poseable arms and head, over 18cm tall
- **72160 Arcanine** – 1,190 pieces – £89.99 / $99.99 / €99.99 – fully poseable display build
- **72168 Rayquaza** – 1,083 pieces – £119.99 / $119.99 / €129.99 – recreates the Sky Pillar scene from Omega Ruby/Alpha Sapphire, includes exclusive Lorekeeper Zinnia minifigure
- **40868 Up-Scaled Red Minifigure** – 930+ pieces – £69.99 / $79.99 / €79.99 – giant poseable Red figure with rotating head and Poké Ball

All five are up for pre-order now on LEGO.com. General release lands from 1st August 2026 via LEGO.com, LEGO Stores and selected retailers, though the big Poké Ball set (72154) holds back until 1st October 2026.

## Why it matters

LEGO Pokémon launched back in March with those large-scale creature builds, all lovely display pieces but no little figures to tell stories with. This is the first time the range has proper minifigures and character figures, which changes the game for anyone who wants to actually build scenes rather than just shelf ornaments. Throw in an exclusive Rayquaza minifigure and a Poké Ball you can genuinely open and close, and this feels like the theme growing up rather than just adding another creature to the collection.

## What to watch next

Worth keeping an eye on retailer stock once 1st August rolls around, big licensed launches like this tend to sell fast. And with minifigures now confirmed as part of the plan, don't be shocked if more Trainers and Pokémon pairs turn up down the line.
